new_paintings.slot: (a) Advent: Chant Year/Learn boards, 'Learn Rorate Cæli before Advent' card; Year board's Advent season
new_paintings.work: The Immaculate Conception of Los Venerables
new_paintings.creator: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo (1617–1682)
new_paintings.commons_search: Murillo Immaculate Conception of Los Venerables Prado
new_paintings.why: Rorate cæli desuper — the heavens dropping down the Just One; Advent's Marian expectation, in the bundle's Spanish Baroque register (cf. the Velázquez Coronation).
new_paintings.alternate: Philippe de Champaigne, The Annunciation (c. 1644) (The Met, CC0 if open access) — if a scene rather than an icon is wanted
new_paintings.licence: Public domain (PD-Art: faithful 2D reproduction of a work whose author died more than 100 years ago)

new_paintings.slot: (b) Sunday · the Holy Trinity: Chant Main board, weekday devotions strip
new_paintings.creator: Jusepe de Ribera (1591–1652)
new_paintings.why: The Throne of Grace (the Father holding the dead Son, the Dove above) — tenebrist palette that sits beside the Caravaggio Entombment and Velázquez Crucifixion.
new_paintings.alternate: Guido Reni, The Holy Trinity (1625–26), Santissima Trinità dei Pellegrini, Rome
new_paintings.licence: Public domain (PD-Art: faithful 2D reproduction of a work whose author died more than 100 years ago)

new_paintings.slot: (c) Monday · the Holy Souls; Occasions 'For Those Who Have Died'; Year board All Souls (Nov 2)
features: Prayer Book: For the Holy Souls
new_paintings.work: The Day of the Dead (Le Jour des morts)
new_paintings.creator: William-Adolphe Bouguereau (1825–1905)
new_paintings.why: Two women in mourning at a grave on All Souls' Day; by the painter of the bundle's Pietà and Flagellation, so the two read as one hand.
new_paintings.alternate: Ludovico Carracci, An Angel Frees the Souls of Purgatory (c. 1610), Pinacoteca Vaticana
new_paintings.licence: Public domain (PD-Art: faithful 2D reproduction of a work whose author died more than 100 years ago)

new_paintings.slot: (d) Tuesday · the Holy Angels: Chant Main board, weekday devotions strip
new_paintings.creator: Pietro da Cortona (1596–1669)
new_paintings.collection: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica (Palazzo Barberini), Rome
new_paintings.why: The guardian angel leading a child by the hand, pointing to heaven: Tuesday's devotion exactly, Roman Baroque.
new_paintings.alternate: Domenico Fetti, The Guardian Angel (c. 1615), Musée du Louvre
new_paintings.licence: Public domain (PD-Art: faithful 2D reproduction of a work whose author died more than 100 years ago)

new_paintings.slot: (e) Wednesday · St Joseph: Chant Main board, weekday devotions strip
new_paintings.work: Saint Joseph and the Christ Child
new_paintings.creator: Guido Reni (1575–1642)
new_paintings.commons_search: Guido Reni Saint Joseph Christ Child Houston
new_paintings.why: Half-length Joseph holding the Child: an icon of the saint that crops well to a tile.
new_paintings.alternate: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, Saint Joseph with the Infant Jesus (c. 1665–66), Museo de Bellas Artes de Sevilla
new_paintings.licence: Public domain (PD-Art: faithful 2D reproduction of a work whose author died more than 100 years ago)

new_paintings.slot: (f) October / Our Lady of the Rosary (Oct 7): Chant Main 'Month of the Holy Rosary' card, Year 'Feast days ahead', Occasions 'A Sung Rosary'
new_paintings.creator: Caravaggio (1571–1610)
new_paintings.commons_search: Caravaggio Madonna of the Rosary Kunsthistorisches
new_paintings.why: St Dominic giving out rosaries at Our Lady's command — the feast's own subject, by the painter of the bundle's Entombment.
new_paintings.alternate: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, The Virgin of the Rosary (c. 1650–55), Museo del Prado
new_paintings.licence: Public domain (PD-Art: faithful 2D reproduction of a work whose author died more than 100 years ago)

new_paintings.slot: (g) Christ the King (last Sunday of October): Chant Year 'Feast days ahead' (Christus Vincit)
new_paintings.work: Christ Triumphant over Sin and Death
new_paintings.creator: Peter Paul Rubens (1577–1640)
new_paintings.collection: Rubens workshop picture; several versions (e.g. Rubenshuis, Antwerp) — pick the version Commons tags PD-Art
new_paintings.commons_search: Rubens Christ triumphant over sin and death
new_paintings.why: The risen Christ enthroned over death, Flemish Baroque beside the bundle's Rubens Descent and Van Dyck Crowning.
new_paintings.alternate: Hans Memling, Christ Surrounded by Musician Angels (c. 1480s), KMSKA Antwerp — earlier style, but the kingship is explicit
new_paintings.licence: Public domain (PD-Art: faithful 2D reproduction of a work whose author died more than 100 years ago)

new_paintings.slot: (g) All Saints (Nov 1): Chant Year 'Feast days ahead' (Litaniæ Sanctorum)
new_paintings.work: Adoration of the Trinity (The Landauer Altarpiece)
new_paintings.creator: Albrecht Dürer (1471–1528)
new_paintings.commons_search: Dürer Landauer Altarpiece Adoration of the Trinity
new_paintings.why: The communion of saints, every state of the Church adoring the Trinity: All Saints in one picture; also a second choice for the Trinity slot.
new_paintings.alternate: Fra Angelico, The Forerunners of Christ with Saints and Martyrs (c. 1423–24), National Gallery, London
new_paintings.licence: Public domain (PD-Art: faithful 2D reproduction of a work whose author died more than 100 years ago)

new_paintings.slot: (h) Prayer Book 'Pray Now' hero for Morning Prayers (On rising)
new_paintings.creator: Jules Breton (1827–1906)
new_paintings.commons_search: Jules Breton The Song of the Lark Art Institute
new_paintings.why: A field-worker stopping at sunrise — the day offered at its start; 19th-c. academic like the Hofmann and Bouguereau already bundled. AIC publishes it CC0.
new_paintings.alternate: Jean-François Millet, The Angelus (1857–59), Musée d'Orsay — but that is the evening Angelus
new_paintings.licence: CC0 1.0 (Art Institute of Chicago open access)

new_paintings.slot: (h) Prayer Book 'Pray Now' hero for Night Prayers (Before sleep); Chapel's Prayer Book tile at night
new_paintings.creator: Georges de La Tour (1593–1652)
new_paintings.commons_search: Georges de La Tour Penitent Magdalen Metropolitan
new_paintings.why: Prayer by a single candle at night — the examination of conscience before sleep. The Met's open-access image is CC0.
new_paintings.alternate: Georges de La Tour, The Magdalen with the Smoking Flame (c. 1640), LACMA

new_paintings.why: Same subject as Night Prayers; an alias saves ~500 KB. If a distinct picture is wanted: Gerrit van Honthorst / Jan Lievens candlelight devotional scenes.

flagged.work: Photograph of Carlo Acutis (head and shoulders, red polo, mountains behind)
flagged.creator: Unknown; the widely circulated family photograph (c. 2005–06)
flagged.licence: Not established — almost certainly in copyright (a modern photograph; the Acutis family / Associazione Amici di Carlo Acutis control the official images)
flagged.note: Used in CarloAcutisView (CachedAssetImage("carlo_acutis")). Do not ship without permission. Replacement options, in order: (1) written permission from the Associazione Carlo Acutis (carloacutis.com) for this photograph; (2) a freely licensed photograph on Commons (fetch.py --search 'Carlo Acutis' lists any, with licence; as of the last check most Commons images of him were deleted as non-free, so expect none); (3) no photograph: the page draws the votive candle or a monogram instead. A painted 'old master' image cannot exist for a saint who died in 2006, so the brief's 'same style' replacement is not possible here.
